newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria ATX posts record close, but well off highs.
newsitem.headline: Austria ATX posts record close, but well off highs.

text.p: Austria's blue-chip ATX index ended at a record closing high for the third session on Tuesday, but was pummelled off earlier highs as a late flurry of profit-taking kicked in.
Traders expect the market to consolidate its gains and say a correction down to below 1,300 points is possible over the short term although the long-term upward trend remains intact.
"A correction was overdue," said one, adding the ATX has room down to around 1,280 points. "The rally happened too quickly, was too euphoric," echoed another.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips closed 1.58 points, or 0.12 percent, higher at 1,310.7 with 10 stocks advancing, 10 falling and one unchanged by the close.
The ATX was earlier driven up to 1,323.19 points on the back of selective demand, particularly in cartonboard maker Mayr-Melnhof, Flughafen Wien, EVN and Boehler.
But traders said that a weak opening in U.S. markets following a three-day holiday weekend encouraged profit-taking with the market at such highs.

Mayr Melnhof was the day's top gainer, surging four percent to 627 schillings. Traders said since the share had broken through key psychological resistance at 600 schillings it could easily extend its bull run over the short term.
"Fundamentally, it's looking really good. There's a lot of optimism for next year," said one trader.
The day's leading decliner was Bank Austria preferred, down 2.07 percent at 436 ATS.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index gained 0.99 points, or 0.21 percent, to 480.55.
The June ATX future closed unchanged at 1,311 points on turnover of 1,095 contracts.
